descricao_original: Serous secretions are released into the lumen of the acinus and continue into intercalated ducts. Intercalated ducts are initially lined by simple squamous epithelium which quickly becomes simple cuboidal. Intercalated ducts are smaller in diameter than the acini. The point where two acini empty into an intercalated duct is visible in this image. 600x

marcadores.explicacao_original: The lining cells of Intercalated ducts add bicarbonate to the secretory product and absorb chloride ions from it. Because it is composed entirely of acini, the parotid has more numerous ducts than the other salivary glands.
